q: What is a polymer?
options: a small molecule made by breaking up a larger molecule
a large molecule built up from many small molecules called monomers
a molecule that contains only one repeating atom
explain: Polymers are long molecules formed by joining many monomer molecules together.

q: Which statement about alkenes is correct?
options: They are saturated hydrocarbons that contain only single bonds.
They are unsaturated hydrocarbons that contain a C=C double bond.
They are unsaturated compounds that contain oxygen.
They are saturated compounds that contain a C=C double bond.
explain: Alkenes are hydrocarbons that contain a C=C double bond, so they are unsaturated.

q: Which is the general formula of the alcohol homologous series?
explain: Alcohols have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH, for example CH₃OH (n = 1) and C₂H₅OH (n = 2).

q: A compound has a name ending in -ene. What type of compound is it?
explain: The ending -ene shows a C=C double bond, so the compound is an alkene.

q: Which list contains only fossil fuels?
explain: The three fossil fuels are coal, natural gas and petroleum. Hydrogen, wood and ethanol are not fossil fuels.

q: Which conditions are used to make ethanol by fermentation of aqueous glucose?
options: an acid catalyst, 25–35 °C and plenty of oxygen
explain: Fermentation uses yeast at 25–35 °C in the absence of oxygen. Air is excluded so the ethanol is not oxidised.

q: Ethanoic acid reacts with magnesium. What are the products?
explain: Like other acids, ethanoic acid reacts with a reactive metal to give a salt and hydrogen. The salt is magnesium ethanoate.

q: Which statement describes the bonding in alkanes?
options: All the bonds are single covalent bonds.
There is one C=C double bond in each molecule.
They contain ionic bonds between carbon and hydrogen.
They contain delocalised electrons between the carbon atoms.
explain: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons that contain only single covalent bonds.

q: How is poly(ethene) formed?
options: Ethanol molecules join together by condensation polymerisation.
Ethane molecules are cracked and then joined.
Many ethene molecules join together by addition polymerisation.
Ethene molecules are oxidised and then joined.
explain: Ethene monomers contain C=C. The double bonds open and the molecules join in long chains to form poly(ethene).

q: What conditions are used to crack large alkane molecules?
options: high temperature and an inert atmosphere only
explain: Cracking breaks long alkane molecules into smaller ones using a high temperature and a catalyst.

q: Which substances are made from polymers?
explain: Plastics are made from polymers.

q: An alkane molecule contains five carbon atoms. What is its molecular formula?
explain: Alkanes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. For n = 5 this gives C₅H₁₂.

q: Which of these names is that of an alcohol?
explain: The ending -ol shows the –OH group of an alcohol. -ane is an alkane, -ene an alkene and -oic acid a carboxylic acid.

q: What is the main constituent of natural gas?
explain: Natural gas is mainly methane, CH₄.

q: Which equation represents the fermentation of glucose?
explain: Glucose gives two molecules of ethanol and two of carbon dioxide, which balances: 6 C, 12 H and 6 O on each side.

q: What is the formula of sodium ethanoate?
explain: Ethanoate is CH₃COO⁻ and sodium is Na⁺, so the salt is CH₃COONa.

q: What are the products of the complete combustion of methane?
explain: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon gives carbon dioxide and water: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.

q: Why do plastics sent to landfill sites cause a problem?
options: Plastics dissolve in rain water and pollute rivers.
Plastics react with soil to form fuels.
Many plastics are not biodegradable, so they remain for a very long time.
Plastics decompose quickly and release oxygen.
explain: Most plastics are unreactive and not broken down by microorganisms, so they persist in landfill sites and take up space.

q: Why are large alkane molecules cracked in oil refineries?
options: to make longer molecules that are more viscous
to make shorter, more useful molecules, including alkenes
to make the molecules less volatile
to remove carbon and hydrogen from the molecules
explain: There is more demand for short-chain fuels and alkenes than for long-chain molecules, so cracking turns the surplus long chains into more useful products.

q: What is a functional group?
options: the carbon chain that gives a compound its boiling point
the number of carbon atoms in each molecule of a compound
a group of atoms that is the same in every organic compound
an atom or group of atoms that determines the chemical properties of a homologous series
explain: The functional group (such as C=C or –OH) is the part of the molecule that decides how the compounds react, so it determines the chemical properties.

q: What is the structural formula of ethanoic acid?
explain: Ethanoic acid has two carbon atoms and the –COOH group, so it is CH₃COOH.

q: Which compound is a hydrocarbon?
explain: A hydrocarbon contains hydrogen and carbon only. The other compounds also contain oxygen or chlorine.

q: What is an environmental problem caused by burning plastics?
explain: Burning plastics can release toxic gases, such as carbon monoxide, so disposal by burning causes pollution.

q: Which conditions are used to make ethanol from ethene and steam?
explain: Ethene and steam react at 300 °C and 6000 kPa (60 atm) with an acid catalyst.

q: Solid sodium carbonate is added to ethanoic acid. What is observed?
options: A gas forms that relights a glowing splint.
A gas forms that burns with a squeaky pop.
Bubbles of gas form that turn limewater milky.
explain: Carbonates react with acids to give a salt, water and carbon dioxide, which turns limewater milky.

q: Which equation represents the complete combustion of methane?
explain: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O has 1 C, 4 H and 4 O on each side. The others are not balanced or do not give CO₂.

q: Which equation shows a possible cracking reaction of decane?
explain: C₁₀H₂₂ → C₈H₁₈ + C₂H₄ balances: 10 C and 22 H on each side. The other equations have unequal numbers of C or H atoms.

q: What is an environmental problem caused by plastics being dumped in the sea?
options: They dissolve and make the sea more acidic.
They quickly rot and use up dissolved oxygen.
They accumulate in the oceans and can harm marine animals.
They form alkenes that kill fish.
explain: Plastics do not rot, so they build up in oceans and can be swallowed or entangle marine animals.

q: Which statement describes a saturated compound?
options: Its molecules contain at least one carbon–carbon double bond.
Its molecules contain no hydrogen atoms.
Its molecules contain the maximum number of carbon atoms.
Its molecules contain only single carbon–carbon bonds.
explain: In a saturated compound all the carbon–carbon bonds are single bonds. Compounds with C=C bonds are unsaturated.

q: A compound has the molecular formula C₄H₁₀. To which homologous series does it belong?
explain: For n = 4 the alkane formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ gives C₄H₁₀. An alkene with four carbons would be C₄H₈.
